amendments.body: The legacy nitrogen kinetics param_meta migration in `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs` (around line 2172-2205) moves metadata verbatim from legacy keys (e.g. `aob_k_tan_mg`) to canonical keys (e.g. `aob_k_tan_mg_n_per_l`) via `move_legacy_process_param_meta_key()`, but the associated `valid_range` and `unit` fields are not transformed to match the new scale. When `legacy_total_param_to_mg_per_l()` converts a whole-tank-total value to a concentration, the metadata's `valid_range` may no longer be semantically correct for the transformed value. Either the migration should also transform `valid_range` bounds by the same scaling factor, or range-checking of migrated legacy parameters should be skipped/warned.
amendments.rationale: A semantic mismatch between the numeric value (now in mg/L concentration) and the metadata range (still in whole-tank mg total) can cause spurious out-of-range warnings or, worse, silently pass range checks that should fail. This only affects legacy TOML files that carry explicit param_meta on the old-style keys, but it is a correctness bug in the migration path.

amendments.body: Five of nine data preset files (`moderate_planted.toml`, `ro_like.toml`, `soft_acidic.toml`, `fast_stem.toml`, `root_rosette.toml`) have file-level provenance sections but completely lack per-parameter `param_meta` entries. Both substrate files (`coarse_porous.toml`, `active_planted.toml`) annotate only `colonizable_area_factor` out of 7+ parameters each. PROVENANCE_STATUS.md already acknowledges this under 'Parameters Not Yet Annotated', but the acceptance criteria require 'representative enriched files from the chemistry, ecology, and shrimp tracks' and currently only `hard_shrimp.toml` and `process/default.toml` qualify as fully representative. Add at least one per-parameter `param_meta` entry to each of the substrate and plant preset files to meet the 'representative file per family' requirement.
amendments.rationale: The acceptance criteria state 'Representative enriched files from the chemistry, ecology, and shrimp tracks load through the G1 schema without special-case hacks.' Plant and substrate presets currently have no per-parameter provenance entries, so they do not demonstrate that provenance metadata works for those parameter families. One or two entries per file would close this gap without requiring exhaustive annotation.

amendments.body: The `low_temp_repro_ramp_width_c` parameter is marked `placeholder` confidence in `neocaridina_davidi.toml` param_meta and PROVENANCE_STATUS.md, yet it is actively used at runtime in `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1583` to shape the cold-side reproduction curve. Per the project's own tier definition, placeholder parameters 'must be resolved before any scientific claim depends on it.' Add a TODO or explicit code comment at the usage site in shrimp.rs noting the placeholder status, so that future callers and scenario authors are immediately warned that the cold-ramp behavior is not literature-backed.
amendments.rationale: The provenance metadata is only visible if someone reads the TOML file or PROVENANCE_STATUS.md. A developer reading shrimp.rs has no indication that this parameter is a placeholder. A single-line comment at the usage site prevents silent dependence on an unvalidated value.

amendments.body: Nitrifier kinetic rate parameters `decomposer_vmax_per_hour`, `decomposer_growth_yield`, `decomposer_decay_rate_per_hour`, and all AOB/NOB/comammox `vmax`, `growth_yield`, and `decay_rate` fields in `process/default.toml` lack `param_meta` entries despite being equally load-bearing for cycling speed as the K_s half-saturation constants that ARE annotated. The acceptance criteria require provenance for 'AOB/NOB/comammox K_s values (nitrogen kinetics)' but the K_s values alone are insufficient — without knowing the confidence of vmax and yield, a calibration bead cannot prioritize which rate constants to tune. Add at minimum a heuristic or placeholder `param_meta` block for each vmax and growth_yield parameter.
amendments.rationale: Half-saturation constants and maximum rates are equally critical for Monod kinetics — knowing one is 'literature' is misleading if the other is an unacknowledged heuristic. The acceptance criteria list nitrogen kinetics as a priority family, and the vmax/yield constants are part of that family.

amendments.body: The `ATMOSPHERIC_CO2_PPM` constant in `crates/tank_core/src/systems/chemistry.rs:17` is hardcoded to 410.0 with no provenance comment. This value directly affects Henry's law CO2 equilibrium calculations and all downstream carbonate chemistry. It should have at minimum a one-line comment noting the source (e.g., NOAA global average ~2020) and that it is treated as a fixed constant for the current model scope.
amendments.rationale: Every other carbonate solver constant (KH_CO2_25C, KH_TEMP_FACTOR_K, pKa1, pKa2) has detailed provenance comments and appears in PROVENANCE_STATUS.md. ATMOSPHERIC_CO2_PPM is a direct peer in importance but is the only one without any provenance annotation.

payload.summary: Reviewed all changes for the tanksim-6e5.7.2 provenance metadata bead. Tests pass. The provenance schema (provenance.rs) is well-designed with proper confidence tier modeling, range validation, and round-trip serialization. The core priority parameters (nitrogen K_s values, carbonate constants, shrimp reproduction/molt/toxicology thresholds, chloride protection factor, plant/algae growth rates, denitrification kinetics) are properly annotated in process/default.toml and neocaridina_davidi.toml with appropriate confidence tiers. PROVENANCE_STATUS.md provides a clear developer-facing summary. Division-by-zero safety is handled via .max(0.01) guards throughout shrimp.rs. Found five actionable issues: (1) a semantic mismatch bug in legacy param_meta migration where valid_range isn't scaled alongside the value transformation, (2) incomplete per-parameter metadata coverage in plant/substrate preset files falling short of the 'representative file per family' acceptance criterion, (3) the placeholder-confidence low_temp_repro_ramp_width_c parameter is used at runtime without any code-site warning, (4) nitrifier vmax/yield/decay rate constants lack param_meta despite being co-critical with the annotated K_s values, and (5) ATMOSPHERIC_CO2_PPM lacks provenance unlike its peer solver constants.
